approach: Extend `check_defined_terms` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs so the names it requires a `Term <name>:` definition for are STRUCTURAL_TERMS plus a new `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES: [&str; 1] = ["Hermes"]`, through one private `named_term` replacing `structural_term`. Every ontology term is classified by mechanism, not by one judgment. A `#[cfg(test)] UNGATED_TERMS` list sits next to `AMBIGUOUS_NAMES`, and each of its entries has a reason. A test requires every `[[term]]` name in docs/ontology.toml to be in exactly one of the two lists, and every listed name to be an ontology term. A term added to the ontology therefore fails the build until someone decides whether readings must define it. The error text tells the reader to say which recorded sense applies and to cite docs/ontology.toml; the one-sense limit is stated in the doc comment and in D165. The unreleased CHANGELOG bullets are corrected in place, and D164 is left alone and amended by an appended D165. The producer writes the corpus tests first and runs them against the unchanged reading.rs to record the failures, then makes the change.

decisions.choice: Gate the class by a two-list partition of the ontology: AMBIGUOUS_NAMES (gated) and a #[cfg(test)] UNGATED_TERMS of (name, reason) pairs. A test asserts every ontology name is in exactly one list, and every listed name exists in the ontology (case-sensitive). Controls: an extra ontology term 'Zeus' is reported as unclassified, a listed 'Zeus' is reported as missing, and a name in both lists is reported.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The ontology's own rule says a term is added only after a misread, so a new term is a candidate for gating. Today a new term would pass every test and never be gated, which is the gap that let 0wtc through. With the partition, adding a term fails the build until the author lists it as gated or ungated with a reason. Ungated entries: planning, job and landed are common words in most requests; Athena is the system's own name, in nearly every request; Sri is a naming convention, not a word a reading must define; 'product versus system' is a phrase the single-word matcher cannot match. UNGATED_TERMS is cfg(test) because only the test reads it, which avoids dead_code under -D warnings.

rejected.option: One-direction sync test (listed names exist in the ontology) plus a prose sentence in D165
rejected.why: It cannot fail when a term is added to the ontology, so it leaves the class open. The 'mechanism' default also forbids prose-only.

rejected.option: Gate every ontology term at run time by reading docs/ontology.toml
rejected.why: job, planning, landed and Athena appear in most requests, so refusals would be constant. The file is not in the plain copy readers see, and the brief puts wiring the ontology into prompts out of scope.

decisions.choice: Add AMBIGUOUS_NAMES beside STRUCTURAL_TERMS and run both through one `named_term` inside the existing `check_defined_terms`. Store the name in ontology case, compare it lowercase, and return the canonical string so the error says `Term Hermes:`. An ambiguous name matches as the exact word or its 's possessive, with no plural stem. The plain-prose filter, the skipped generated lines and the three-word rule are reused.
decisions.reason: The need is the same: a word whose meaning the reading must state before work builds on it. The filter, skips, definition parsing and the step line already exist and are tested. The fault starts in the one gate that turns wording into a reading.

rejected.option: A new check_ambiguous_names step in refusing_check
rejected.why: It duplicates the prose filter and definition parsing, and needs new step-order and every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case entries for no gain.
The misread is the bare name. 'Hermes' alone, the Orchestration god, is the other sense and needs a definition too.
The error would say `Term hermes:`, which does not match the ontology name, and the sync test could not compare exactly.

decisions.choice: Do not make the Term line for an ambiguous name require a citation of docs/ontology.toml. Instead the error says the line must state which recorded sense applies and cite docs/ontology.toml, and the doc comment and D165 state the limit: the check forces a restatement but cannot verify that the restatement matches the recorded senses.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2 with the finding's own minimum option. Criterion 1 says a Term Hermes line of three or more words is accepted, and a citation requirement would contradict it. The error text is tested for the sense and citation wording.

rejected.option: Accept an ambiguous-name Term line only if it cites docs/ontology.toml
rejected.why: It contradicts criterion 1 as written and still would not prove the sense is right; a citation can sit beside the wrong sense.
